newsitem.title: TURKEY: Amnesty kicks off Turkey rights abuses campaign.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty kicks off Turkey rights abuses campaign.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday kicked off a worldwide drive to highlight human rights abuses in Turkey similar to previous efforts focused on China and Sudan.

"This is a campaign for Turkey. This is a campaign to ensure that the necessary safeguards will be put in place to protect the rights of people in detention," Amnesty chief Pierre Sane told Reuters before the campaign's launch at a news conference.

The European Parliament last month threatened to withhold hundreds of millions of dollars in European Union aid to Turkey, complaining that Ankara has not carried out promises to clean up its rights record.

Sane said the London-based group would pressure international organisations in a bid to expose Turkey's poor record on torture, extrajudicial killings and the recent phenomenon of suspects "disappearing" in custody.
Successive Turkish governments, the judiciary and even doctors have turned a blind eye to "gross" human rights abuses by the powerful security forces, Amnesty said in a report released on Tuesday.
"What concerns us most is the increase in the number of disappearances, the number of extrajudicial executions," Sane said.
